applicable_when: The kernel has 168 registers/thread — far above the ~64-96 typical for well-tuned GEMM kernels. This crushes occupancy to 6.25% (only 1 active warp/scheduler) and leaves 69.5% of cycles with no eligible warp. The B-matrix load uses a broken transposed index pattern (tl.broadcast_to(idx_m + 1024*idx_n, ...)) that causes 8-way shared memory bank conflicts (59.58% potential speedup). Replacing manual pointer arithmetic with tl.make_block_ptr + tl.advance (block pointer API) maps to TMA hardware on Hopper: (1) offloads address generation from SMs, (2) fixes the B-matrix access pattern to be coalesced, (3) reduces register pressure by eliminating per-element index computations, and (4) enables async software pipelining via num_stages > 1 to hide memory latency. Adding @triton.autotune explores BLOCK_M/N/K and num_stages to find the optimal configuration for this 1024x1024x1024 GEMM on H200.
